scope: Primary-document and SDK-source audit plus local SDK request fixture; not a GCS service experiment.

sdk.fetched_source_matches_installed: Yes, byte-for-byte after removing the single final newline added by the local apply_patch transfer.

source_sections.finding: A populated Blob generation is appended as a generation selector when constructing its download URL.
The same download response supplies generation and metageneration saved in Blob properties.
The non-chunked raw download consumes a transport response and passes that response to header extraction.

documents.finding: Successive object versions have unique generation values, which need not increase. Metageneration starts at 1 within each generation and advances for metadata changes.
documents.role: Fresh allocation; do not substitute monotonic order or metageneration alone.

documents.finding: Ordinary uploaded objects are immutable; replacement is atomic and changes generation.
documents.role: Stored bytes remain fixed for one finalized ordinary generation.

documents.section: Object Versioning example; Object Versioning reference; Restoration behavior
documents.finding: Deleting the live version leaves no live version, even when older versions remain. Copying a noncurrent version to the live name allocates a new generation. Metadata-only example keeps generation.
documents.role: No historical head reactivation by ordinary delete/restore operations.

documents.finding: Soft-delete restoration creates a copy with a new generation and metageneration 1.
Restored copies receive new generation values.
documents.role: Additional document check; not an executed service test.

documents.finding: A moved object receives a new generation and metageneration 1.
documents.role: Additional document check; distinguished from HNS folder rename. The main proof lists its smaller surveyed operation set.

documents.section: Strongly consistent operations; Cache control and consistency; Atomic operations
documents.finding: Object read-after-write/delete is strong, but cached public reads can be stale. Request cache bypass is ignored. Individual-object operations are atomic; batches are not.
documents.role: Point-read contract and cache exclusion; no multi-object transaction claim.

documents.finding: Built-in caching requires public accessibility. Proxies and clients can cache independently. Private and no-store have different cache scopes.
Eligible gzip objects can be decompressed according to metadata; Accept-Encoding:gzip requests stored compressed data instead.
documents.role: Stored-byte observation requires a fixed raw representation and disabled client decompression.

documents.finding: alt=media returns object data. generation chooses a particular revision instead of the default latest object. A precondition is distinct from that selector.
documents.role: Current-name observations must not silently select historical revisions.

documents.finding: GET returns object data and can select a generation explicitly.
The response generation identifies the accessed data version; metageneration identifies its metadata version.
Bucket generation identifies an incarnation of the bucket independently of its reused name.
documents.role: Motivates fixed bucket lifetime; no claim that a separate bucket GET is atomically bound to object GET.

documents.section: Restoring objects with duplicate paths; project restoration discussion
documents.finding: HNS folder renames can produce same-name/same-generation collisions. Project restoration can restore previously live buckets.
documents.role: Explicitly exclude HNS namespace moves and authority-level restoration.

documents.finding: Hierarchical folder renames move paths without copying underlying objects.
documents.role: Do not extend the fixed flat-namespace proof to HNS.

documents.finding: Rapid Bucket supports appending without full rewrites and requires hierarchical namespace.
documents.role: Exclude appendable objects; restrict to ordinary finalized immutable objects.

limitations: Documentation was read at the listed date; no immutable server-document snapshots are claimed.
Official SDK source is commit-pinned; dependency versions and local results are archived.
No Google Cloud account, endpoint, service write, or service read was used.
The operation-level no-return proof is conditional on the documented contract and scope; a finite model is not an implementation verification.
